reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes paid cryptocurrency packages as a way to make money while repeatedly encouraging viewers to recruit others, create multiple accounts, and build a six-person team. It presents tiered commissions and escalating package purchases as producing cash flow, token growth, and a blueprint to reach $100,000 in six months, making participation dependent on recruitment and further payments rather than an ordinary standalone product sale.

citations.quote: if you invite others you're gonna make a whole lot more money
you have to be a pro trader
you want to get six people to follow you within this system six people to commit
those tokens are going to turn into one coins

opening.argument: Judge the financial claims by their wording. The speaker does not tell every viewer to buy the largest package: he says, "whatever you can afford is best," and identifies a lower-cost starting point for someone whose "money is tight." His discussion of future coin prices is framed as a possibility, not an observed return: "let's say ten dollars twenty dollars fifty dollars." Those qualifications do not establish that the opportunity is sound, but they matter when deciding whether this presentation makes an unconditional promise of earnings.

citations.quote: whatever you can afford is best
that's the best way to get started if your money is tight
let's say ten dollars twenty dollars fifty dollars

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to recruitment and higher package tiers, but "if you're going to build a team" presents team-building as a conditional path, while the speaker also says viewers can make money without inviting anyone. A description of possible commissions is not, by itself, proof that every viewer must recruit or that the stated returns are guaranteed.

citations.quote: if you're going to build a team
if you don't want to invite anybody and as you as you create more cash flow and you upgrade your packages it's going to help you make more money anyway

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Affordability advice is not a meaningful warning about losing money. The speaker urges viewers to buy packages, saying "the higher the package the more you're gonna benefit," and presents recruitment as the way to increase earnings. Conditional language about future prices does not undo the paid, tiered recruitment pitch.

citations.quote: the higher the package the more you're gonna benefit
if you invite others you're gonna make a whole lot more money
the tycoon Trader which is 5,500 euro's so you can benefit off for generations

opening.argument: This is substantially a walkthrough of a compensation system. The speaker introduces it as instruction on "how to work through those packages," explains who counts as a first generation, and uses an illustrated three-account diagram to show the arrangement. A judge can recognize that the lesson discusses potential payments without treating every explanation of a commission structure as proof that a viewer was deceived. The visible diagram and the speaker's step-by-step examples establish what is being taught; they do not establish that any depicted payment was actually received.

citations.quote: I want to show you how to work through those packages.
if you sign that person up that is your first generation
so here is a person that came in with the 3,000 and 300 euro package

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening cites inviting others, trader levels, and six-person teams. Those are indeed subjects of the walkthrough, but the speaker's stated purpose is to teach how the packages and network operate. The cited token-conversion statement likewise describes a proposed sequence; it does not show a completed conversion or realized gain.

citations.quote: I wanna teach you we've got a brand new packages that showed up.
those tokens are going to turn into one coins

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is itself the sales pitch. The description directs viewers to join, and the speaker tells them to create three accounts, buy packages, and teach recruits to repeat the setup. Illustrated examples do not make those instructions neutral education.

citations.quote: JOIN THE MILLIONAIRE TEAM !!!! Join: https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/BlackDiamonds.
you want to have 3 accounts ASAP
teach your people you're gonna share this video with your people to ensure they creating three accounts just like you

opening.argument: The video openly describes package prices and a referral-style bonus: the speaker says the temporary extra 10% means buyers "get more tokens" when signing up, then explains percentages associated with people a participant signs up. That is a promotion whose terms the viewer can hear, not evidence in this record that an actual buyer was denied tokens or a stated commission. Even the illustrated earnings examples are presented as examples. The existence of paid tiers and referral rewards warrants scrutiny, but it does not independently verify that the offered tokens or payments were fictitious.

citations.quote: for the next two weeks they're gonna be giving you a extra 10% when you sign up in a package so that means you're gonna get more tokens
when you start at the trader level and above you are going to get a 10% bonus on everybody in your first generation
so here is a person that came in with the 3,000 and 300 euro package

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening accurately identifies multiple accounts, recruitment, and tiered commissions. What it does not establish is that any depicted commission was actually paid, that a viewer incurred a loss, or that the offered tokens did not exist. The speaker describes a purchase and gift-code redemption process, but the record does not independently show its outcome. Those limits matter when moving from an aggressive referral promotion to a finding of deception.

citations.quote: we gonna send you the quotes you gonna send the money and then they got a time ran a senior to the actual gift code so you can redeem the gift code from your log in

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is more than an incidental referral reward. The speaker directs viewers to fund three accounts to qualify for binary pay, says one recruit can generate payments to two of those accounts, and urges each recruit to build the same structure. The absence of a documented victim or failed payout in this video does not change what the video is promoting.
